subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this umbrella remain the canonical Windows gateway-down tracker, or should maintainers split it now into separate lifecycle, config-repair, pricing, Browser, and CLI-backend issues before implementation?
rationale: The source confirms several reported gaps, but the requested end state crosses stable gateway runtime, CLI recovery, optional Browser plugin isolation, Windows service supervision, and product UX choices that automation should not prioritize or scope alone.

options.title: Keep umbrella, split owned fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical parent while maintainers create or assign narrower fix/proof items for each affected boundary.

options.title: Choose one urgent first fix
options.body: Keep this open but explicitly prioritize only the Windows ensure/single-instance/relaunch path before other subproblems.

options.title: Require live repro before splitting
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or Windows proof confirms which reported modes still reproduce on current main.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, split owned fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical parent while maintainers create or assign narrower fix/proof items for each affected boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent source-history overlap across gateway lifecycle, pricing startup, config schema, and stale-process handling.
